book_title: Pop's Farm, Bakery, and Sunday Memories

chapters.title: Growing Up on the Farm
chapters.photo_idea: a yellow school bus on a dirt road

sentences.text: Pop grew up on a small farm outside of town.
He had two cows, about thirty chickens, and a dog named Biscuit.
Every morning at six o'clock, Pop walked down the dirt road to wait for the school bus.
It was a yellow bus, and it was always late.
Pop never minded, because his best friend Tommy waited with him, and they would count the crows on the fence.
In the winter of 1958, the snow was so deep that the bus did not come for three days.
They were not upset about that at all.

chapters.title: Working at the Bakery
chapters.photo_idea: fresh rolls in a corner bakery

sentences.text: Pop's first job was at the corner bakery when he was fourteen.
Mr. Alvarez paid Pop one dollar a week, plus all the day-old bread he could carry home.
Pop was not a very good baker.
When Pop burned the first batch of rolls, Mr. Alvarez did not yell at him.
He just laughed and said everybody burns the first batch.
Pop worked there for two summers.
He still remembered the smell of cinnamon when he opened the door at five in the morning.

chapters.title: Sunday Dinners at Grandmother's
chapters.photo_idea: a family sitting around a dinner table with plates of food

sentences.text: Every Sunday, Pop's whole family came to his grandmother's house for dinner.
There were eleven of them around one table that was only built for eight.
His uncle Joe always told the same joke, and everyone always laughed anyway.
Pop's grandmother never let anyone leave without a plate of food to take home.
Pop did not know it then, but those Sunday dinners were the best part of his childhood.
If Pop could go back to one day, it would be one of those Sundays.
